documents_mark_paid.description: Mark a document as paid (full payment recorded).

documents_record_refund.description: Record a refund against a document (full or partial): records only, moves no money. PAYMENT STATUS ONLY: it does not issue a credit note, and a partial marks the document 'partial' while a full one marks it 'refunded'. A refund or cancellation taken in Shopify already auto issues the matching credit note, so check documents_for_orders before adding one by hand. On a split order (goods plus software) record the refund against the document that actually carries the refunded line.

documents_convert_to_invoice.description: Convert a quote or proforma into an invoice. For a quote linked to a Shopify draft order (shopify_draft_order_id set) this COMPLETES the draft order in Shopify with payment pending (the B2B customer pays by wire against the invoice, no Shopify email goes out), Shopify creates the real order, the quote becomes 'invoiced' with the order id and number, and the invoice is issued automatically by the order-created auto-flow moments later (threshold gated like any store invoice). Returns mode 'shopify_order_created' in that case: do NOT call invoice_create_and_issue afterwards, the invoice arrives on its own; find it with documents_for_orders or documents_search on the order number. A quote or proforma without a draft order is converted locally (mode 'local') and the new invoice is returned. Gated for agents (approval card); a human clicking Convert in the UI confirms a dialog and needs no approval. The quote's po_number is carried onto the invoice.

operation_category.description: E-invoicing: the operation category of the invoice (goods, services or mixed) when the source quote or proforma does not state one. A French business e-invoice needs it stated; omit it to keep the source's.

notes.description: Non financial metadata, max 2000 characters, editable at any status (on a draft and on an already issued, sent or paid document alike). Null or an empty string clears it. Omit it to carry the source quote or proforma's own notes onto the invoice.

documents_convert_local.description: Convert a quote or proforma with no Shopify draft order into an invoice, in one commit. Called by documents_convert_to_invoice only.

credit_note_create_and_issue.description: Create a credit note, a legal document, and issue it in one call. A credit note is a first-class legal document — its own gap-free CN-{YYYY}- number series, issued straight to 'issued' status (never a payable document — no due date, no mark_paid). Lines carry NEGATIVE unit_price_minor mirroring what is reversed on the original invoice, and the total must come out negative.

operation_category.description: E-invoicing: the operation category, goods, services or mixed. Omit it on a credit note against an e-invoice to keep the original's category; otherwise required when the credit note is an e-invoice to a French business.

issuer_profile_id.description: Issuer profile id to issue under. Optional — omitted defaults to the org's default issuer profile (single-issuer orgs).

counterparty.description: The customer the credit note is issued TO (normally the same customer as the original invoice). legal_name, country, address and email are ALL required — a credit note cannot be issued to an unnamed, unaddressed or unreachable recipient. country is the ISO-3166 alpha-2 code — it drives the tax classification (domestic / intra-EU / export), re-derived exactly like an invoice.

billing_line1.description: E-invoicing: first line of the buyer's structured billing address (street).

billing_line2.description: E-invoicing: second line of the buyer's structured billing address, if any.

billing_postcode.description: E-invoicing: the buyer's billing postcode. An e-invoice to a French business needs postcode, city and country code.

billing_country_code.description: E-invoicing: the buyer's billing country, ISO-3166 alpha-2 (e.g. FR). Defaults to the counterparty country when omitted.

contact_id.description: Kernel contact id of the customer if known, else null.

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency of the document (e.g. EUR, USD). Defaults to EUR when omitted; should normally match the original invoice's currency.

incoterm.description: Incoterm for the document (EXW/FCA/FOB/CIF/DAP/DDP/DPU). Defaults to DAP.

issued_at.description: Issue date, ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today in the issuer's time zone. A date before the last number of that series is refused (issue_date_before_last_number), so is a date before the invoice it corrects (issue_date_before_original), and so is a date after today (issue_date_in_future).

original_document_id.description: The id of the invoice this credit note corrects/reverses. When set, MUST reference an existing document of type='invoice' (validated before issuance — an id for a quote/proforma/PO/other credit note is rejected). Persisted onto external_refs.original_document_id; the original invoice's lifecycle_log gets a `credit_note_issued` entry naming this credit note. Omit for a credit note with no linked original (rare — most credit notes correct a specific invoice).

reason.description: Free-text reason for the credit note (e.g. 'partial return — 2 of 10 units', 'pricing correction'). Persisted onto external_refs.reason and rendered on the PDF under the original-invoice reference line.

po_number.description: The customer's purchase order number. Printed as a "PO number" line on the credit note PDF and indexed for documents_search. When omitted and `original_document_id` is set, it is inherited automatically from the original invoice's own po_number.

notes.description: Non financial metadata, max 2000 characters, editable at any status (on a draft and on an already issued, sent or paid document alike). Null or an empty string clears it.

items.description: The credit note's line items. unit_price_minor is NEGATIVE, mirroring the portion of the original invoice being reversed.

unit_price_minor.description: Unit price in MINOR currency units (cents) — NEGATIVE to mirror the reversed amount, e.g. -41940 for -€419.40. NOT a major-unit float.

tax_rate_bp_override.description: Optional per-line tax rate in basis points (2000 = 20%); omit to inherit the document's classified rate.

hs_code.description: Harmonized System tariff code for this line, e.g. 9207.90.

customs_description.description: Plain-language customs goods description for this line.

country_of_origin.description: ISO country of origin for this line.

product_source.description: Optional catalog source for this line ('shopify' or 'manual').

external_id.description: Optional catalog id for this line, paired with product_source.

credit_note_issue.description: Issue a credit note from a draft (drafts_create with type='credit_note'). Handler-conditional gating against issuer.invoice_approval_threshold_minor (unset means always approve, threshold 0; a credit note with no original_document_id is ALWAYS approved), compared against the ABSOLUTE VALUE of the credit note's grand total. When the draft's external_refs.original_document_id references an invoice, that invoice's lifecycle_log gets a `credit_note_issued` entry on success.

order_reissue_apply.description: Reissue an invoice after a Shopify order edit changed the LINE SET or the AMOUNTS (an order edit that only touches address, notes, tags, or fulfilment does NOT call this). ALWAYS GATED, one human approval covers BOTH documents together: a credit note that fully reverses the original invoice, and a replacement invoice carrying the order's current items and amounts, issued only once the human signs off. Do NOT call credit_note_create_and_issue and invoice_create_and_issue separately for an order-edit reissue: this tool exists precisely so the operator sees and approves both documents as ONE decision. PAYMENT: any payment already recorded stays on the ORIGINAL invoice; the credit note reverses that invoice as a legal document, and the REPLACEMENT invoice is issued UNPAID (nothing is auto-transferred or auto-marked paid, so re-applying the payment or refunding the difference is a separate, deliberate step). This is invoked by the invoicing app's own onShopifyOrderUpdated handler when the order's billing signature diverges from what was last invoiced; it is not meant to be called ad hoc with an unrelated items list. Do NOT documents_mark_paid the replacement to simulate transferring the payment: re-applying it or refunding the difference is a deliberate, separate decision. The original's po_number is carried onto BOTH the credit note and the replacement.

original_document_id.description: The issued invoice this order edit diverged from.

shopify_order_id.description: The Shopify order the replacement invoice links to (same order the original billed).

shopify_order_number.description: The order's human name (e.g. '#1149'), carried onto the replacement invoice.

billing_signature.description: Identifies WHICH order edit this approval answers (not interpreted beyond that).

dedupe_key.description: shopify_order_id + billing_signature. A repeated webhook delivery for the SAME edit computes the identical value so the kernel collapses it into the existing pending approval instead of stacking a duplicate; a later, different edit produces a different value and raises a fresh one.

currency.description: Defaults to the original invoice's currency when omitted.

reason.description: Free text reason for the credit note; defaults to a standard order-edit reissue note.

notes.description: Non financial metadata, max 2000 characters, editable at any status (on a draft and on an already issued, sent or paid document alike). Null or an empty string clears it. Applied to BOTH the credit note and the replacement invoice; omit it to carry the original invoice's own notes onto both.

items.description: The order's CURRENT (post-edit) line items, carried onto the replacement invoice.

hs_codes_assign.description: Assign HS code + country-of-origin + customs description to a product. Accepts a dotted code (e.g. "9207.90") or plain digits; the code is normalised to digits-only before it is stored, so the library never ends up holding the same code in two formats. Use hs_codes_unassign to clear an assignment and fall back to the Shopify value instead.

hs_codes_unassign.description: Clear a product's customs overlay, restoring the Shopify value. By default clears every overlay field (hs_code, country_of_origin, customs_description) and removes the overlay entry entirely, so the product falls back to a live Shopify variant lookup at document build time. Pass fields to clear only some of them and keep the rest as recorded. Use this to undo a prior hs_codes_assign.

fields.description: Which overlay fields to clear. Omit to clear all of them (this removes the overlay row).

hs_codes_library_upsert.description: Create or update an entry in the shared HS-code library (a code plus its description), independent of any single product. The code is normalised to digits-only before it is stored; if that normalised code already exists in the library under a different format, the existing entry is updated in place rather than creating a duplicate. Use this to seed or correct the library, not to assign a code to a product (use hs_codes_assign for that).

hs_codes_library_delete.description: Delete an entry from the shared HS-code library by code. Refuses and reports how many products still reference the code unless force is true, since deleting it does not touch those products' overlays. Use hs_codes_unassign first if the intent is to stop a product from using the code, then delete the library entry once nothing references it.

force.description: Delete even if products still reference this code. Defaults to false.

settings_issuer_profile_create.description: Create an issuer profile. Setting any bank or control field (iban, swift_bic, bank_name, approval thresholds, require_two_eyes, auto_email_enabled, mail_account_id) needs invoicing:issuer:admin.

iban.description: Payout bank account printed on every invoice. Changing it is a gated action and needs invoicing:issuer:admin.

swift_bic.description: Payout BIC printed on every invoice. Changing it is a gated action and needs invoicing:issuer:admin.

bank_name.description: Payout bank name printed on every invoice. Changing it is a gated action and needs invoicing:issuer:admin.

invoice_approval_threshold_minor.description: Approval threshold in minor units; 0 or unset means every issuance is approved. Changing it needs invoicing:issuer:admin.

mail_account_id.description: Mailbox invoices are sent from. Changing it needs invoicing:issuer:admin.

timezone.description: IANA time zone of this issuer's issue dates and number years, e.g. Europe/Paris. An unknown name is refused (issuer_timezone_invalid). UTC chosen on purpose is stored as Etc/UTC. Left unset, dates follow the organization's time zone, then UTC.

prices_include_tax.description: Typed unit prices INCLUDE tax (gross). Must match the Shopify shop's 'include tax in prices' setting when the profile is mapped to a shop: prices you type on a quote line are then tax inclusive, and the document shows the net amount plus the VAT it contains. Off: typed prices are net and tax is added on top.

settings_issuer_profile_update.description: Update an issuer profile by id. Changing any bank or control field (iban, swift_bic, bank_name, approval thresholds, require_two_eyes, auto_email_enabled, mail_account_id) needs invoicing:issuer:admin; the other fields need only invoicing:settings:write.

iban.description: Payout bank account printed on every invoice. Changing it is a gated action and needs invoicing:issuer:admin.

swift_bic.description: Payout BIC printed on every invoice. Changing it is a gated action and needs invoicing:issuer:admin.

bank_name.description: Payout bank name printed on every invoice. Changing it is a gated action and needs invoicing:issuer:admin.

invoice_approval_threshold_minor.description: Approval threshold in minor units; 0 or unset means every issuance is approved. Changing it needs invoicing:issuer:admin.

mail_account_id.description: Mailbox invoices are sent from. Changing it needs invoicing:issuer:admin.

timezone.description: IANA time zone of this issuer's issue dates and number years, e.g. Europe/Paris. An unknown name is refused (issuer_timezone_invalid). UTC chosen on purpose is stored as Etc/UTC. Left unset, dates follow the organization's time zone, then UTC.

prices_include_tax.description: Typed unit prices INCLUDE tax (gross). Must match the Shopify shop's 'include tax in prices' setting when the profile is mapped to a shop: prices you type on a quote line are then tax inclusive, and the document shows the net amount plus the VAT it contains. Off: typed prices are net and tax is added on top.

settings_issuer_profile_delete.description: Delete an issuer profile by id. Needs invoicing:issuer:admin (the profile's bank and control settings go with it).

documents_update.description: Edit an issued document. A draft, including one in the month-end run, is edited with drafts_update. Once an INVOICE or a CREDIT NOTE is ISSUED its FINANCIAL SUBSTANCE is FROZEN: `lines`, `tax_treatment`, `counterparty_name`, and `counterparty_vat_id` can no longer be changed in place (the call fails `issued_document_immutable`).

approvalCard.summary: Edit document {{params.id}} (recipient, address, dates, notes or lines)

counterparty_shipping_address.description: Counterparty shipping (ship to) postal address, freeform and multi-line.

counterparty_shipping_name.description: Falls back to counterparty_name when null.

counterparty_country.description: Counterparty's ISO-3166 country code. Correcting this does NOT automatically re-derive tax_treatment for an already-issued document's totals (issue-time classification is not re-run on edit) — pass `tax_treatment` explicitly if the correction should also change the recorded treatment label.

issued_at.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). On a draft, null clears it. On an issued document it stays in the number's year; an issued invoice or credit note's date also stays between its neighbouring numbers and on or before today.

due_at.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD), or null to clear.

po_number.description: The customer's purchase order number. Non financial reference metadata, editable on a draft AND on an already-issued document (like address/email/incoterm/dates); the edit is logged and the PDF is re-rendered with the new value. Null clears it.

notes.description: Non financial metadata, max 2000 characters, editable at any status (on a draft and on an already issued, sent or paid document alike). Null or an empty string clears it.

customer_reference.description: Editable at any status. Null or an empty string clears it.

lines.description: REPLACES every line on the document. Omit this param entirely to leave lines untouched. When provided, subtotal_minor/tax_total_minor/grand_total_minor are recomputed from these lines (each line's tax_rate_bp_override, else the document's classified rate). Under an issuer profile with prices_include_tax on, unit_price_minor here is treated as GROSS (tax included) and is divided down to net before storage, every time this is called, with no way to tell a freshly typed price apart from an echoed one. So a line read back from documents_get is ALREADY NET: never echo those values back unchanged in a future call. Read the others back only to know what they are, then resend the lines you actually mean as newly typed gross prices — or better, omit `lines` from the call entirely when none of them changed.

unit_price_minor.description: Unit price in MINOR units (cents), e.g. 41940 for 419.40, or "41940". NET of VAT, unless the issuer profile has prices_include_tax: then it is GROSS and the net is derived at the document's VAT rate. A reverse charge or export document charges no VAT, so nothing is netted. The approval card states which.

tax_rate_bp_override.description: Optional per-line tax rate in basis points (2000 = 20%); omit to inherit the document's classified rate.

customs_description.description: Plain-language customs goods description for this export line.

country_of_origin.description: ISO country of origin for this line (export/customs).

product_source.description: Optional catalog source for this line ('shopify' or 'manual'). Paired with `external_id`, links the line to a catalog product so customs enrichment fills in whatever this line leaves blank; an explicit hs_code/country_of_origin/customs_description on the line ALWAYS wins over the overlay.

external_id.description: Optional catalog id for this line (e.g. a Shopify variant gid), paired with `product_source`.

documents_retry_pdf.description: Re-render a document's PDF (when pdf_status is failed).

documents_preview_pdf.description: Resolve a document's rendered-PDF file id + inline URL for preview.

documents_download_pdf.description: Resolve a document's rendered-PDF file id + URL for download.

einvoicing_classify.description: THE tool for 'can I e-invoice this customer / this order, and why?': always call it for that question. E-invoicing regime (e_invoice, e_reporting, out_of_scope, needs_review) with its reasons, and what the issue gate would refuse and which tool fixes it. Pass exactly one of document_id (a draft is computed; an issued document returns its recorded regime), shopify_order_id (the invoice that order would get, or its issued invoice's regime) or contact_id (an invoice to that counterparty). Read only.

shopify_order_id.description: A Shopify order id (numeric or gid).

counterparty_identity_get.description: The e-invoicing identity of a counterparty: customer kind, SIREN / SIRET and whether the SIREN is confirmed against the business registry, registry name and head office, territory treatment. Pass contact_id, or document_id (a document linked to no contact returns its buyer snapshot). Read only. It shows the stored identity only: to answer whether a customer, an order or a document is e-invoiced and why, call einvoicing_classify.

counterparty_identity_lookup.description: Look a French company up in the official business registry (recherche-entreprises.api.gouv.fr) by name, SIREN or SIRET, optionally narrowed to a postcode. With contact_id, a French VAT id on file is turned into its SIREN first and every candidate says whether its registered name matches the counterparty. Returns candidates (siren, names, head office, active or ceased, legal category); it NEVER picks one: choose the one that is this counterparty, then record it with counterparty_identity_set. Use this, never a web page, as the source of a SIREN; a web search may only point you to the name to look up. Read only.

counterparty_identity_set.description: Record a counterparty's e-invoicing identity: customer_kind (business, individual, public_entity, non_registered_entity), SIREN / SIRET, with its provenance (source registry when picked from counterparty_identity_lookup, vat_derived when read off a French VAT id, agent_web with source_url when found on the web, manual when typed by a person). A SIREN is re-checked against the registry and written at once only when the registry returns it active under the counterparty's own name; otherwise (another company's name, no registry answer, registry down, a ceased company, or replacing a confirmed SIREN) it returns pending_approval and nothing is written until a person confirms. Kind-only changes are written at once. customer_kind records who the buyer really is (a company is business): never a way past an issue refusal. Billing address fields apply only to a draft linked to no contact (document_id). Recording the identity re-runs the orders waiting on it.

document_id.description: A draft linked to no contact.

counterparty_territory_set.description: Administrator decision for a buyer whose territory is not decided automatically (Monaco, overseas departments and collectivities): treat it as French (as_fr) or foreign (as_foreign), with the reason. Gated: a person approves it.

einvoicing_settings_set.description: Change the organisation's e-invoicing settings: gate_mode (enforce refuses an e-invoice whose data is missing; warn issues it and records the warning), cibs_switch_date (YYYY-MM-DD, the date the legal mentions switch to the new tax code references), provider_app (the installed app that is the e-invoicing platform), cutover_date (YYYY-MM-DD, invoices issued from this date are sent or booked), send_enabled and book_enabled. Gated: a person approves it.

approvalCard.summary: E-invoicing settings: gate mode {{params.gate_mode}}, switch date {{params.cibs_switch_date}}, platform {{params.provider_app}}, cut-over {{params.cutover_date}}, sending {{params.send_enabled}}, booking {{params.book_enabled}}

provider_app.description: The installed app that is the organisation's e-invoicing platform (PA).

cutover_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD: invoices issued from this date are sent / booked.

legal_originals_verify.description: Check that the stored legal originals (the exact file of each issued invoice and credit note's first render, the Factur-X for an e-invoice, and imported legacy originals) are intact: recomputes each file's fingerprint and compares it with the one recorded when it was fixed. Returns how many were checked and intact, and lists any that no longer match or cannot be read. Pass document_id for one document. Continue with next_offset until it is null. Read only.

document_id.description: Only the legal originals of this document (its uuid).

limit.description: Legal originals checked per call, default 20, at most 50.

offset.description: Where to continue: the next_offset of the previous call.

einvoicing_readiness.description: What still blocks e-invoicing, by counterparty and draft: each item names its subject (contact_id and/or document_id, label), the blocker_code (the same code the issue gate refuses with), the one action that fixes it (action.tool, action.label, action.params_hint) and the date of the counterparty's last document. Most recent first. An empty list means nothing blocks. Separately, issuer_time_zones_to_choose lists each issuer nobody chose a time zone for: it blocks nothing (dates follow the organization's zone, then UTC), so ask which zone once and set it with settings_issuer_profile_update (timezone; UTC on purpose counts). Read only. It lists what blocks e-invoicing across customers: to answer whether one customer or order is e-invoiced and why, call einvoicing_classify.

limit.description: Items returned, default 50, at most 200 (count is always the total).

einvoicing_backfill_identities.description: Backfill the e-invoicing identity of every existing customer: the customer kind its documents support, the SIREN read off a French VAT id and confirmed against the business registry (written only when the registry returns that company active under the customer's own name; anything else is left for einvoicing_readiness), the structured billing address of its latest document and open drafts from their printed address, and the issuer's SIREN / SIRET from a valid registration id. Never changes an identity a person or a registry check recorded. dry_run (default true) reports the counts and writes nothing. At most `limit` registry checks per call (default 20, at most 50): continue with next_cursor until it is null. Gated: a person approves each call.

limit.description: Registry checks in this call, default 20, at most 50.

einvoicing_backfill_legacy_originals.description: Record the legal original of every imported legacy document: the PDF the importer stored, hashed (SHA-256) and copied onto its own legal-original record, and point back at that file any imported document whose PDF a later re-render replaced. dry_run (default true) reports the batch (processed, repointed, remaining) and reads or writes nothing. Works in batches: at most `limit` documents (default 10, at most 50) and, past the first, at most `max_bytes` read (default 5000000, at most 10000000); run again while remaining is above 0. Documents already recorded are never selected again. A document whose imported file cannot be read is set aside (recorded on the document, counted in set_aside, not in remaining) so later batches move past it; retry_failed: true takes the set-aside documents again. Gated: a person approves each call.

approvalCard.summary: Record the legal originals of imported documents (dry run: {{params.dry_run}})

dry_run.description: true (default): report only, read and write nothing.

limit.description: Documents in this batch, default 10, at most 50.

max_bytes.description: Bytes read in this batch past its first document, default 5000000, at most 10000000.

retry_failed.description: true: also take the documents set aside after a failed read (default false).

invoicing-overview.description: How to use the Invoicing app with Liaison
invoicing-overview.body: The Invoicing app issues and tracks invoices, quotes, proformas, purchase orders and credit notes for your contacts. There is no draft category: invoices are issued automatically from paid Shopify orders (or by converting a quote or proforma), credit notes from refunds, and only quotes, proformas and purchase orders are started by hand. A quote is a Shopify draft order when the issuer profile is mapped to the shop: create the draft order (Shopify admin, quote_create_and_issue, or ask the agent) and the numbered quote PDF appears here; edit or delete the draft order and the quote follows; Convert to invoice completes the draft order with payment pending, Shopify creates the order and the invoice is issued on its own. Numbering model: a per (issuer, type, year) sequence is allocated gap-free at ISSUE time, so the issued sequence is contiguous by construction and a true gap would be anomalous; drafts are unnumbered, so discarding a draft never consumes a number. Reversals: credit_note is a first class document type numbered from its own CN-{YYYY}- series; ask the agent to issue one against the original invoice for the LEGAL document, and record a refund against the original invoice for the PAYMENT status side (a clean reversal normally does both). Set up a routine to chase overdue invoices, and keep payment terms and tax facts in Knowledge so the agent fills documents correctly. Historical invoices stay queryable by the agent for reconciliation. A refund or a cancellation in Shopify issues the credit note by itself, and an order edit that changes lines or amounts raises one approval covering a credit note plus a replacement invoice, so an issued invoice is never edited in place. The customer's purchase order number rides on the document as po_number, printed on the quote, invoice, proforma and credit note, amendable after issue and searchable.

vendor-invoice-to-pennylane.description: Route a supplier/vendor invoice PDF into Pennylane as a supplier invoice.
vendor-invoice-to-pennylane.body: To get a vendor invoice into Pennylane: 1. Find the email + its PDF attachment with mail__search (filter by the supplier/sender) and read it. 2. Import the attachment to a kernel file id (the mail attachment plumbing) so you have a file_id. 3. Call pennylane__supplier_invoice_upload with the file_id + supplier metadata (name, invoice_date, amount_minor, currency). This tool is GATED and only STAGES the document with a manual-upload instruction — it does NOT silently post to Pennylane, and if Pennylane's upload endpoint is unavailable it degrades to 'staged, drop it in Pennylane yourself' rather than claiming success. Tell the user it is staged and pending their approval; never claim the invoice was filed. Money is minor-units.
